findings.title: Valueless `?fbclid` and empty `?fbclid=` set trackingParams.fbclid to null/"" instead of leaving the field absent; `?fbclid=` persists "" to users.fbclid
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §5.1: "New output fields, all absent when their source is absent (never `null`/`\"\"` fabrication — repo rule 10)"; SPEC §8 constraint 1: "Nil for absent, everywhere"; §5.1 cookie rule treats a present-but-empty value as absent. AMBIGUITY NOTED: §4's fbclid row says "the same handling `adct` gets from `sanitizeTrackingValue`" — the existing adct guard (`parsedParams.adct !== undefined`, utils.js:88-90) produces exactly this null/"" behavior, so the implementation is analog-exact; and §4 Notes scope the non-empty-string "present" test to the conditional rules (fbc construction, li_fat_id/gclid fallbacks) only, stating no consequence for fbclid storage itself. The spec is internally in tension; needs a ruling.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js:119-125 (committed a0d59115d): `if (parsedParams.fbclid !== undefined) { trackingParams.fbclid = sanitizeTrackingValue(parsedParams.fbclid, ATTRIBUTION_IDENTIFIER_MAX_LENGTH); }`. Empirically verified with the repo's query-string v6.1.0: `parse('?fbclid')` → `{fbclid: null}` and `parse('?fbclid=')` → `{fbclid: ""}` — both pass the `!== undefined` guard. `sanitizeTrackingValue(null)` returns null (isString fails); `sanitizeTrackingValue("")` returns "". Downstream for `?fbclid=`: AuthForm.tsx:88 / SignupForm.tsx:74 send `fbclid: ""` → useSession.ts variables → apiPost/allKeysToSnake (values untransformed) → sign_up_params[:fbclid] == "" → magic_create/#create persist users.fbclid = "" (no validation, no server-side scrubbing), later copied to organizations.fbclid by organizations_controller.rb:39. Downstream for `?fbclid`: JSON null → Rails nil → column nil (DB end-state matches absent; only the helper output contract is violated). The SSO path is unaffected (GoogleSSOButton.tsx:101 guard `typeof fbclid === "string" && fbclid.length > 0` suppresses the hidden input). The fbc construction correctly excludes both cases (utils.js:135-143).
findings.recommendation: Either (a) guard fbclid storage on the first-occurrence value being a non-empty string (the §4-Notes present test: select first-of-array, then `typeof x === "string" && x.length > 0` before assigning — the `fbclidParamValue` local already computed for fbc at utils.js:135 can be reused), making `?fbclid` and `?fbclid=` produce an absent field; or (b) obtain a ruling that analog-exact adct behavior is intended and record it in the spec. Material persistence difference is only the `?fbclid=` → `""` column case; the `?fbclid` → null case violates the §5.1 output contract but ends nil in the DB.
